title: Your Body Language May Shape Who You Are
titleZh: 肢体语言如何塑造你自己
speaker: Amy Cuddy
desc: 社会心理学家 Amy Cuddy 讲「姿势反馈」：两分钟的高能量姿势如何改变睾酮与皮质醇，让你在压力场合真的更自信。语速偏快、情绪饱满，适合练语调。

cues.en: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast
cues.zh: 翻译人员: Yang Xu 校对人员: Yuguo Zhang

cues.en: So I want to start by offering you a free no-tech life hack, and all it requires of you is this: that you change your posture for two minutes.
cues.zh: 首先我想要提供给你们一个免费的非科技的人生窍门你只需这样做改变你的姿势二分钟时间

cues.en: But before I give it away, I want to ask you to right now do a little audit of your body and what you're doing with your body.
cues.zh: 但在我要把它告诉你们之前，我想要请你们就你们的身体和你们身体的行为做一下自我审查

cues.en: So how many of you are sort of making yourselves smaller?
cues.zh: 那么你们之中有多少人正蜷缩着自己?

cues.en: Maybe you're hunching, crossing your legs, maybe wrapping your ankles.
cues.zh: 或许你现在弓着背，还翘着二郎腿?或者双臂交叉

cues.en: Sometimes we hold onto our arms like this.
cues.zh: 有时候我们像这样抱住自己

cues.en: Sometimes we spread out. (Laughter) I see you.
cues.zh: 有时候展开双臂(笑声)我看到你了(笑声)

cues.en: So I want you to pay attention to what you're doing right now.
cues.zh: 现在请大家专心在自己的身上

cues.en: We're going to come back to that in a few minutes, and I'm hoping that if you learn to tweak this a little bit, it could significantly change the way your life unfolds.
cues.zh: 我们等一下就会回溯刚刚的事希望你们可以稍微改变一下这会让你的生活变得很不一样

cues.en: So, we're really fascinated with body language, and we're particularly interested in other people's body language.
cues.zh: 所以，我们很真的很执着于肢体语言特别是对别人的肢体语言感兴趣

cues.en: You know, we're interested in, like, you know — (Laughter) — an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink,
cues.zh: 你看，我们对(笑声)尴尬的互动，或一个微笑或轻蔑的一瞥，或奇怪的眨眼

cues.en: or maybe even something like a handshake.
cues.zh: 甚至是握手之类的事情感兴趣

cues.en: Narrator: Here they are arriving at Number 10.
cues.zh: 解说员:他们来到了唐宁街10号，看看这个

cues.en: This lucky policeman gets to shake hands with the President of the United States.
cues.zh: 这位幸运的警员可以和美国总统握手噢，还有

cues.en: Here comes the Prime Minister -- No. (Laughter) (Applause) Amy Cuddy: So a handshake, or the lack of a handshake,
cues.zh: 来自....的总理?不(笑声) (掌声)(笑声) (掌声)Amy Cuddy:所以一个握手，或没有握手

cues.en: can have us talking for weeks and weeks and weeks.
cues.zh: 我们都可以大聊特聊一番

cues.en: Even the BBC and The New York Times.
cues.zh: 即使BBC和纽约时报也不例外

cues.en: So obviously when we think about nonverbal behavior, or body language -- but we call it nonverbals as social scientists -- it's language, so we think about communication.
cues.zh: 我们说到肢体行为或肢体语言时我们将之归纳为社会科学它就是一种语言，所以我们会想到沟通

cues.en: When we think about communication, we think about interactions.
cues.zh: 当我们想到沟通，我们就想到互动

cues.en: So what is your body language communicating to me?
cues.zh: 所以你现在的身体语言正在告诉我什么?

cues.en: What's mine communicating to you?
cues.zh: 我的身体又是在向你传达什么?

cues.en: And there's a lot of reason to believe that this is a valid way to look at this.
cues.zh: 有很多理由让我们相信这些是有效的社会科学家花了很多时间

cues.en: So social scientists have spent a lot of time looking at the effects of our body language, or other people's body language, on judgments.
cues.zh: 求证肢体语言的效果或其它人的身体语言在判断方面的效应

cues.en: And we make sweeping judgments and inferences from body language.
cues.zh: 而我们环视身体语言中的讯息做决定和推论

cues.en: And those judgments can predict really meaningful life outcomes like who we hire or promote, who we ask out on a date.
cues.zh: 这些结论可以预测生活中很有意义的结果像是我们雇用谁或给谁升职，邀请谁出去约会

cues.en: For example, Nalini Ambady, a researcher at Tufts University, shows that when people watch 30-second soundless clips of real physician-patient interactions,
cues.zh: 举例而言，Tufts大学的研究员，Nalini Ambady表示人们观赏一部医生和患者互动的30秒无声影片

cues.en: their judgments of the physician's niceness predict whether or not that physician will be sued.
cues.zh: 他们对该医生的和善观感可用来预测该复健师是否会被告上法庭

cues.en: So it doesn't have to do so much with whether or not that physician was incompetent, but do we like that person and how they interacted?
cues.zh: 跟这个医生能否胜任工作没有太大关系重点是我们喜不喜欢他和他们是如何与人互动的?

cues.en: Even more dramatic, Alex Todorov at Princeton has shown us that judgments of political candidates' faces in just one second predict 70 percent
cues.zh: 进一步来说，普林斯顿的Alex Todorov 表示我们对政治人物脸部的喜好判断大概可用来对美国参议院和美国州长的

cues.en: of U.S. Senate and gubernatorial race outcomes, and even, let's go digital, emoticons used well in online negotiations
cues.zh: 竞选结果做70%的预测甚至就网络上在线聊天时使用的表情符号

cues.en: can lead you to claim more value from that negotiation.
cues.zh: 可以帮助你从交谈中得到更多信息

cues.en: If you use them poorly, bad idea. Right?
cues.zh: 所以你千万别弄巧成拙，对吧?

cues.en: So when we think of nonverbals, we think of how we judge others, how they judge us and what the outcomes are.
cues.zh: 当我们提起肢体语言，我们就想到我们如何论断别人别人如何论断我们以及后果会是什么

cues.en: We tend to forget, though, the other audience that's influenced by our nonverbals, and that's ourselves.
cues.zh: 我们往往忘记这点，受到肢体动作所影响的那群观众就是我们自己

cues.en: We are also influenced by our nonverbals, our thoughts and our feelings and our physiology.
cues.zh: 我们也往往受自己的肢体动作，想法感觉和心理所影响

cues.en: So what nonverbals am I talking about?
cues.zh: 所以究竟我说的是怎样的非语言?

cues.en: I'm a social psychologist. I study prejudice, and I teach at a competitive business school, so it was inevitable that I would become interested in power dynamics.
cues.zh: 我是一位社会心理学家，我研究偏见我在一所极具竞争力的商业学院上课因此无可避免地对权力动力学感到着迷

cues.en: I became especially interested in nonverbal expressions of power and dominance.
cues.zh: 特别是在非语言表达对权力和支配的领域

cues.en: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
cues.zh: 权力和支配的非语言表达究竟是什么?

cues.en: Well, this is what they are.
cues.zh: 嗯，让我细细道来

cues.en: So in the animal kingdom, they are about expanding.
cues.zh: 在动物王国里，它们和扩张有关

cues.en: So you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space, you're basically opening up.
cues.zh: 所以你尽可能的让自己变大，你向外伸展占满空间，基本上就是展开

cues.en: It's about opening up.
cues.zh: 关于展开，我说真的

cues.en: And this is true across the animal kingdom.
cues.zh: 透视动物世界，这不仅局限于灵长类

cues.en: It's not just limited to primates.
cues.zh: 透视动物世界，这不仅局限于灵长类

cues.en: And humans do the same thing. (Laughter) So they do this both when they have power sort of chronically, and also when they're feeling powerful in the moment.
cues.zh: 人类也干同样的事(笑声)不论是他们长期掌权或是在某个时间点感到权力高涨他们都这么做

cues.en: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
cues.zh: 特别有趣的原因是它让我们明白权力的展现从来是如此地一致，不管古今世界

cues.en: This expression, which is known as pride, Jessica Tracy has studied.
cues.zh: 这种展现，被认为是一种荣耀Jessica Tracy研究表示

cues.en: She shows that people who are born with sight and people who are congenitally blind do this when they win at a physical competition.
cues.zh: 视力良好无碍和先天视障的人在赢得比赛时都做了同样的事

cues.en: So when they cross the finish line and they've won, it doesn't matter if they've never seen anyone do it.
cues.zh: 当他们跨过终点线赢得比赛之际无论能否看的见他们都做这样的动作

cues.en: They do this.
cues.zh: 他们都做这样的动作

cues.en: So the arms up in the V, the chin is slightly lifted.
cues.zh: 双臂呈V字型朝上，下巴微微抬起

cues.en: What do we do when we feel powerless?
cues.zh: 那我们感到无助的时候呢?我们的行为正相反

cues.en: We do exactly the opposite.
We close up. We wrap ourselves up.
cues.zh: 我们封闭起来。我们把自己蜷起来

cues.en: We make ourselves small.
We don't want to bump into the person next to us.
cues.zh: 让自己变得小一点，最好别碰到别人

cues.en: So again, both animals and humans do the same thing.
cues.zh: 这再一次证明，人类和动物都做同样的事

cues.en: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
cues.zh: 这就是当你有力量和没力量时的行为所以当力量来临时

cues.en: So what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other's nonverbals.
cues.zh: 所以当力量来临时我们会迎合别人的非语言

cues.en: So if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller. We don't mirror them.
cues.zh: 若有人之于我们相对权重时我们倾向把自己变得较小，不会模仿他们

cues.en: We do the opposite of them.
cues.zh: 我们做和他们正相反的事情

cues.en: So I'm watching this behavior in the classroom, and what do I notice?
cues.zh: 当我在课堂上观察这么现象时

cues.en: I notice that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power nonverbals.
cues.zh: 你猜我发现什么?我发现MBA的学生真的很会就充分利用肢体语言

cues.en: So you have people who are like caricatures of alphas, really coming into the room, they get right into the middle of the room before class even starts, like they really want to occupy space.
cues.zh: 你会看到有些人像是统治者走进房间，课程开始之前一屁股坐在正中间好像他们真的很想占据整个教室似的

cues.en: When they sit down, they're sort of spread out.
cues.zh: 当他们坐下的时候，身体会展开

cues.en: They raise their hands like this.
cues.zh: 像这样举手

cues.en: You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in. As soon they come in, you see it.
cues.zh: 有些人则不然他们一走进来你就会发现

cues.en: You see it on their faces and their bodies, and they sit in their chair and they make themselves tiny, and they go like this when they raise their hand.
cues.zh: 从他们的脸和身体你会发现他们坐在椅子上的时候把自己变得很萎靡然后举手的时候是这种姿势

cues.en: I notice a couple of things about this.
cues.zh: 我观察到很多事情

cues.en: One, you're not going to be surprised.
cues.zh: 其中一件，不令人惊讶

cues.en: It seems to be related to gender.
cues.zh: 就是跟性别差异有关

cues.en: So women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
cues.zh: 女人比男人更容易出现这种状况

cues.en: Women feel chronically less powerful than men, so this is not surprising.
cues.zh: 女人一般比较容易比男人感到无力这并不太令人意外。然而我发现的另一件事是

cues.en: But the other thing I noticed is that it also seemed to be related to the extent to which the students were participating, and how well they were participating.
cues.zh: 这并不太令人意外。然而我发现的另一件事是这似乎也跟学生参与的程度高低有关

cues.en: And this is really important in the MBA classroom, because participation counts for half the grade.
cues.zh: 就MBA的课来说这真的非常重要因为课堂参与程度要占成绩的一半

cues.en: So business schools have been struggling with this gender grade gap.
cues.zh: 所以商学院一直以来都为此伤脑筋
